claims.text: Combinatorial sputter deposition can produce a continuous composition spread in HfNbTaTiZr.
Small deviations from equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr will cause systematic variation in mechanical properties.
Increasing the concentration of an element that strengthens through increased lattice distortion will increase hardness.
Increasing the concentration of an element that strengthens through increased lattice distortion will increase yield strength.
Composition-driven increases in strength may compromise ductility.
Nearly equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr produced by conventional methods is a single-phase alloy.
A HfNbTaTiZr thin-film library with controlled composition variations can be fabricated by gradient sputter deposition.
Deposition conditions can be selected that preserve a single-phase high-entropy structure across the composition gradient.
Local mechanical properties of the gradient films can be tested at ambient temperature using nanoindentation and micro-tensile testing.
The single-phase homogeneous structure will persist despite local composition variations.
Changes in individual-element concentrations alter local lattice distortion.
Changes in individual-element concentrations alter solid-solution strengthening.
Changes in lattice distortion and solid-solution strengthening modify dislocation mobility.
Modified dislocation mobility affects hardness, yield strength, and ductility.
Increasing the concentration of a high-modulus element is expected to increase hardness by approximately 5–15%.
Increasing the concentration of a high-modulus element is expected to increase yield strength by approximately 5–15%.
Mechanical-property trends will correlate with modified local chemical environments.
The observed behavior in thin films may not extrapolate to bulk HfNbTaTiZr or high-temperature conditions.
